newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end lower on blue chip declines.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end lower on blue chip declines.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks ended their month-long rise on Wednesday to close lower mainly on profit-taking in pricey blue chips, which brokers said could kick off a correction.
The all share index closed 2.20 points lower at 745.60. The last time the index eased was on March 20 when it fell 0.3 points to 632.7.
Commercial Bank fell 10 rupees to 210, Development Finance Corporation, Hatton national Bank 22.25 to 287.75, Lanka Orix Leasing five to 200.
"Th decline was expected as blue chips had risen very fast on thin volumes," said Rohan Fernando of CT Smith Stock Brokers.
Turnover was 263.5 million rupees led by foreign buying of one million shares of Asian Hotels, 250,000 John Keells Holdings and 40,000 National Development Bank.
Colombo shares, which have risen nearly 23 percent this year due to improved investor sentiment, should soon see a correction due to profit-taking, brokers said.
"Even if there is a correction the index should not ease much due to continuing buying interest," said Dihan Dedigama of John Keells Stock brokers.
